name: The example
expr: (lambda it, cap: (lambda r: (lambda ok: [ok, ok and sum(it[i][0] for i in r) <= cap, sum(it[i][1] for i in r) if ok else None])(len(set(r)) == len(r) and all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < len(it) for i in r)))(list(pack(list(it), cap))))(*args)
show: pack([(3, 4), (4, 5), (2, 3)], 7): [valid positions?, within the bag?, total value]
why: [True, True, 9]: items 0 and 1 weigh 7 and are worth 9. The answer [0, 1] is checked by its facts, so any best choice passes.

show: pack([(6, 30), (3, 14), (4, 16), (2, 9)], 10): [valid positions?, within the bag?, total value]
why: [True, True, 46]: items 0 and 2 weigh 10 exactly. Taking the best value per kilogram first gives items 0 and 1, worth only 44.

expr: (lambda it, cap: (lambda r: (lambda ok: [ok, ok and sum(it[i][0] for i in r) <= cap, sum(it[i][1] for i in r) if ok else None])(len(set(r)) == len(r) and all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < len(it) for i in r)))(list(pack(list(it), cap))))(*args)

why: [True, True, 9]: room for two items, so take the two most valuable.

name: Each item once
expr: (lambda it, cap: (lambda r: (lambda ok: [ok, ok and sum(it[i][0] for i in r) <= cap, sum(it[i][1] for i in r) if ok else None])(len(set(r)) == len(r) and all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < len(it) for i in r)))(list(pack(list(it), cap))))(*args)
show: pack([(1, 10), (5, 12)], 3): [valid positions?, within the bag?, total value]
why: [True, True, 10]: item 0 can be taken only once. A list with 0 three times is not a valid answer.

name: 100 items, bag of 2,500
expr: (lambda it, cap: (lambda r: (lambda ok: [ok, ok and sum(it[i][0] for i in r) <= cap, sum(it[i][1] for i in r) if ok else None])(len(set(r)) == len(r) and all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < len(it) for i in r)))(list(pack(list(it), cap))))(*args)
show: pack(100 items, 2500): [valid positions?, within the bag?, total value]
why: Trying all 2¹⁰⁰ choices is impossible. Fill the table, keep every row (or a record of each choice), then walk back from the last row (lesson 9).

name: 200 items, bag of 3,000
expr: (lambda it, cap: (lambda r: (lambda ok: [ok, ok and sum(it[i][0] for i in r) <= cap, sum(it[i][1] for i in r) if ok else None])(len(set(r)) == len(r) and all(type(i) is int and 0 <= i < len(it) for i in r)))(list(pack(list(it), cap))))(*args)
show: pack(200 items, 3000): [valid positions?, within the bag?, total value]
why: 201 rows of 3,001 cells. To walk back, compare each row with the one above: a change means the item was taken.
